correctness.rationale: Write rank-one T=uv*, ||v||=1, a=v*u, s=|a|², L=||u||². T²=aT and defining 2-partial-isometry identity reduce exactly to L(2−s)=1 (0≤s<2). Orthogonal component b=u−av has ||b||²=(s−1)²/(2−s). S=vw* with w=2u−La v and w*u=1 gives idempotents ST=P=vv* and TS=Q=uw*. For same positive bounded invertible G, two remaining Penrose equations are GP=PG and GQ=Q*G; these imply Gv=gv, Gu=cw, yielding g=c(2−L) when a≠0 and Gb=2cb. Therefore positivity requires L<2 (the a=0 exception automatically has L=1/2). G₀=(2−L)P+2(I−P) suffices; for a,b nonzero its forced eigenvalues give sharp cond 2/(2−L)=2(2−s)/(3−2s), while s=0,1 admit G=I. Endpoint s=3/2 gives explicit 2×2 T and S with (TS)(ST)=0 but (ST)(TS)≠0, forbidding any common orthogonal-projection metric. Independent sample s=1.2 yields cond=8/3 and correct Hermiticity; endpoint exact commutator contradiction. Proof works in infinite dimension; script finite tests are not infinite proof.
